title: U.S. House · Kentucky's 5th District
area: Eastern Kentucky and Appalachia, including London, Hazard and Middlesboro.

context.text: The Democratic primary was canceled and Ned Pillersdorf advanced without opposition.

candidates.name: Hal Rogers
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 19, 2026 Republican primary, defeating Kevin Smith, Benjamin Hurley, Brandon Monhollen and Jerry Shelton.

summary.text: Hal Rogers is the Republican incumbent for Kentucky's 5th Congressional District, having served since 1981. He is an attorney and chairs the House Appropriations Subcommittee on Commerce, Justice, Science and Related Agencies.

background.text: Earned his A.B. and LL.B. from the University of Kentucky in 1962 and 1964, after attending Western Kentucky University from 1956-1957.
Served in the Kentucky and North Carolina Army National Guard from 1956 to 1963.
Worked as an attorney in Kentucky's Pulaski and Rockcastle counties before his political career.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Appropriations and chairs its Subcommittee on Commerce, Justice, Science and Related Agencies (119th Congress, 2025-2026).
Chaired the Appropriations Subcommittee on Commerce, Justice, Science in the 118th Congress (2023-2024); previously chaired the full Appropriations Committee (2011-2016).

candidates.name: Ned Pillersdorf
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Democratic primary without opposition after the primary was canceled.

summary.text: Ned Pillersdorf is a Democratic candidate for Kentucky's 5th Congressional District, an Eastern Kentucky attorney who says he has run a "poverty volume" law practice for 44 years. He opposes cuts to Medicaid, Medicare, food stamps and other safety-net programs, and criticizes incumbent Hal Rogers's vote for the 2025 reconciliation tax law.

background.text: Says he has practiced law in Eastern Kentucky for 44 years, focused on low-income clients, and has been involved with several nonprofits.

priorities.text: "If you support the ongoing proposed slashing of: Medicaid, Medicare, food stamps, funds to help low income folks pay their utilities, and the defunding of public television, public radio, job corp, cancer research, etc – all so the billionaire class can get a deficit busting tax break – I don't expect to persuade you to support my candidacy."

positions.summary: Opposes cuts to Medicaid and Medicare, criticizing incumbent Hal Rogers's support for reductions to those programs.
positions.quote: I truly fear for our vulnerable neighbors here in Appalachia.

summary.text: Gerardo Serrano is an independent candidate for Kentucky's 5th Congressional District, a small-business owner and farmer who says he became active in politics after experiencing civil asset forfeiture. He campaigns as independent of both major parties, focused on constitutional rights and due process.

background.text: Says he was born in Chicago and has lived in Kentucky's 5th District for over 25 years, working as a small-business owner and farmer.

priorities.text: "I am independent—not controlled by either political party, political insiders, or special interests. I will answer to the people of Kentucky's 5th District, demand transparency, oppose wasteful omnibus bills, and insist that Congress vote on major issues openly and individually."

positions.summary: Says he will defend the Second Amendment as part of a broader commitment to constitutional rights and due process.
positions.quote: I will defend due process, privacy, the Second Amendment, and Congress's constitutional responsibility to decide when America goes to war.

summary.text: Mikel Wein is an independent candidate for Kentucky's 5th Congressional District from Letcher County. He campaigns on ending corporate control of Eastern Kentucky's land and energy resources, a national healthcare system, and reducing U.S. military spending abroad.

background.text: Says he lives in Letcher County on land that has been in his family for over a century.

priorities.text: "Eastern KY deserves to end the decades of corporate and monopoly control of its land, energy, and natural wealth, and chart its own future."

positions.summary: Supports a national healthcare system that prioritizes people over profit.
positions.quote: a national healthcare system that prioritizes people over profit

positions.summary: Says he supports halting U.S. military support for other countries, including Israel, over allegations of human rights abuses.
positions.quote: halt military support for other countries, such as Israel, that commit genocide or other crimes against humanity

positions.summary: Says he supports defunding ICE, describing its activities as unlawfully harming people.
positions.quote: de-fund services, such as ICE, that are unlawfully harming people in our own country and making us afraid.

summary.text: Billy Ray Wilson is an independent write-in candidate for Kentucky's 5th Congressional District. No detailed public statements or biographical profile beyond his name on the ballot were found for this candidate.
